_meta.why_v2: Ground-up rebuild, installed from an owner-supplied rewrite per audit/REWRITE-INSTALL-KIT.md. The v1 five-mode design (spiral/unfreeze/recover/reflect/patterns — severity scoring, an automatic breathing banner, cognitive-distortion labels, nervous-system explanations, recovery protocols, episode/trigger pattern analysis) is gone entirely, replaced with one job: separate what happened from what the visitor's mind added (pinned to a PREDICTION/INTERPRETATION/CONCLUSION enum), name what's genuinely unknown, and offer at most one grounded next move. Recurring-pattern recognition across time is deliberately NOT this tool's job any more — that's Before the Crash. The v1 cases below (de-spiral-work-email-catastrophizing, de-recover-burnout-crash) tested endpoints and fields (action: spiral/recover, distortion_label, stages, permissions, recovery_signs) that no longer exist and have been replaced wholesale, not diffed.
_meta.why_v2_1: Live verification of v2 surfaced the CONTRACT's own heavy use of the word 'visitor' (in field descriptions like "the visitor's words", plus prompt headers VISITOR'S LOOP / VISITOR'S OPTIONAL FACTUAL ANCHOR) leaking into the model's actual output as third-person voice — 'The visitor is scared their choices have fallen behind' instead of 'You're scared your choices have fallen behind' — the same class of bug already fixed once this session on SomeoneSaidItBetter. Fixed by adding an explicit VOICE section to CONTRACT with a wrong/right example pair, renaming the prompt's own section headers away from 'VISITOR'S', and rewriting every schema field description to say 'addressed as you/your' instead of 'the visitor's'. Re-verified live: all three cases below now render consistent second-person voice end to end.
_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden spiral-stopper). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation, SENSITIVE mental-health domain. GUARDS: validateResult() in backend/routes/spiral-stopper.js keys on top-level `safety_redirect` (boolean) being present; caps what_happened<=3, what_the_spiral_added<=4, what_is_unknown<=4; pins what_the_spiral_added[].status to the fixed PREDICTION/INTERPRETATION/CONCLUSION enum (unrecognized value falls back to INTERPRETATION, never crashes); next_move.available requires a genuine non-empty action string, never a placeholder. A true safety_redirect returns ONLY {safety_redirect:true, message} with every other field forced to its empty/null shape — ordinary analysis fields never coexist with a safety redirect. DO NOT reverse: the enum whitelist, the array caps, the safety_redirect field-zeroing, or the no-inner-double-quote rule (NO_QUOTE_RULE) on all quote-heavy fields.

input.thoughts: Ich habe meinem Chef eine E-Mail mit einem peinlichen Tippfehler geschickt und jetzt bin ich sicher, dass er denkt, ich bin unprofessionell und inkompetent. Wahrscheinlich erwähnt er das bei meiner nächsten Bewertung und ich verliere die Beförderung, auf die ich seit Monaten hinarbeite.
input.actual_event: Ich habe eine E-Mail mit einem Tippfehler an meinen Chef geschickt.

what_happened: Du hast eine E-Mail mit einem Tippfehler an deinen Chef geschickt.

what_the_spiral_added.thought: Dein Chef denkt jetzt, du bist unprofessionell und inkompetent.
what_the_spiral_added.grounded_version: Du weißt nicht, was dein Chef über die E-Mail denkt oder ob er den Tippfehler überhaupt bemerkt hat.

what_the_spiral_added.thought: Er wird das bei deiner nächsten Bewertung erwähnen.
what_the_spiral_added.grounded_version: Ob dieser Tippfehler jemals in einer Bewertung eine Rolle spielen wird, ist dir nicht bekannt.

what_the_spiral_added.thought: Du verlierst die Beförderung, auf die du seit Monaten hinarbeitest.
what_the_spiral_added.grounded_version: Der Ausgang deines Beförderungsprozesses ist offen. Ob dieser Tippfehler daran irgendetwas ändert, steht nicht fest.

what_is_unknown: Ob dein Chef den Tippfehler bemerkt hat.
Wie dein Chef die E-Mail insgesamt wahrgenommen hat.
Ob der Fehler bei deiner Bewertung oder Beförderungsentscheidung irgendeine Rolle spielen wird.
Was dein Chef aktuell über deine Arbeit denkt.
output.anchor: Du hast eine E-Mail mit einem Tippfehler geschickt. Was daraus folgt, ist im Moment noch unbekannt.

next_move.action: Wenn es sich inhaltlich anbietet, kannst du eine kurze Folge-E-Mail schicken, die den Tippfehler beiläufig korrigiert oder die korrekte Information liefert.
next_move.why: So weißt du, dass du das Mögliche getan hast, ohne die Sache größer zu machen als sie ist.

output.after_this: Die Frage, ob das Auswirkungen auf deine Beförderung hat, musst du jetzt nicht lösen.

input.thoughts: My best friend has not texted me back in four days after I told her some hard news about my marriage. She always replies fast. I keep thinking she is pulling away from me, that she is judging me, that she probably talked to her husband about how messy my life has become, and that our friendship is basically over now.
input.actual_event: I have not heard back from my friend in four days.

what_happened: You shared hard news about your marriage with your best friend.
She has not replied in four days.
Her usual pattern is to reply quickly.

what_the_spiral_added.thought: She is pulling away from you.
what_the_spiral_added.grounded_version: She has not responded yet. Whether that means distance is not established.
You do not know what she is thinking or feeling about what you shared.

what_the_spiral_added.thought: She probably talked to her husband about how messy your life has become.
what_the_spiral_added.grounded_version: You do not have any information about what she has or has not said to anyone.
Four days of silence is the only thing you can point to right now. That is not enough to establish where the friendship stands.

what_is_unknown: Why she has not replied — you do not know her reason.
What she is thinking or feeling about what you told her.
Whether something unrelated to you is occupying her right now.
What her silence means for the friendship going forward.
output.anchor: Your friend has not replied in four days after you shared something hard — and right now, that is all you actually know.

next_move.action: Send her one short, low-pressure message — something like: 'No rush, just wanted to check in on you.' This keeps the door open without demanding a response.
next_move.why: It gives her a clear, easy way to re-engage and removes any chance that she is simply unsure whether you need space too.

output.after_this: You do not need to figure out the future of this friendship before she has even had a chance to respond.

input.thoughts: I cannot stop thinking about hurting myself right now. Everything feels pointless and I do not think I can keep myself safe tonight.

output.message: You're in a really hard place right now, and you don't have to figure anything else out tonight except staying safe. Please reach out right now: call or text 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, free, 24/7) or text HOME to 741741 (Crisis Text Line). If you feel you cannot keep yourself safe in the next few minutes, call 911 or go to your nearest emergency room. If there is someone who can physically be with you right now — a friend, family member, neighbor — please contact them too.
